trust_decision.summary: Which bytes of an untrusted HTTP/1.1 request define message framing (header name boundaries, Transfer-Encoding vs Content-Length, body end) is decided in the shared Java wire parser BodyAndHeaderParser.parseHeaders/chunkedContent, plus a request-only framing check in the Scala server wrapper's headerComplete.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'request smuggling'; the server-side headerComplete hook already holds framing checks (obs-fold at :114-123), so an engineer adds TE/CL checks there; the summary's 'Java wire parser' points second to BodyAndHeaderParser.java.

fix_sites.entry_point: BlazeServerBuilder HTTP/1.1 server -> Http1ServerStage.reqLoopCallback -> parser.doParseHeaders -> headerComplete (reject Transfer-Encoding together with Content-Length; fix.diff:170-175)

Same server route, plus BlazeClient response parsing (BlazeHttp1ClientParser.finishedHeaders) and the public Java API Http1ServerParser/Http1ClientParser.parseHeaders: non-tchar field-name chars and colon-less lines rejected (fix.diff:55-58, 75-78)
fix_sites.module_kind: shared low-level Java parser (public API, used by server and client)

fix_sites.entry_point: Same shared parseHeaders: 'Transfer-Encoding: identity' no longer silently ignored, rejected as unsupported (fix.diff:218-230)
New helper isTchar used by the field-name loop (fix.diff:90-115)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: http/src/main/java/org/http4s/blaze/http/parser/BodyAndHeaderParser.java:181-251 (shared Java parser in module 'http', also reached by blaze-client via blaze-client/src/main/scala/org/http4s/blaze/client/BlazeHttp1ClientParser.scala:71-72)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The server wrapper already hosts the framing checks (Http1ServerParser.scala:114-123), so a solver puts every check there and argues the shared Java parser is also the client's response parser and must stay lenient (ClientParserSuite.scala:255-273 asserts 'Transfer-Encoding: identity' is accepted).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Header lines with a colon but an empty value ('Name:', 'Name: ', 'Name:\t') must still parse to an empty value; only the colon-less line is rejected. Duplicate Content-Length with identical value is still accepted by the Java parser. A fix that rejects empty values or all repeated Content-Length breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: field-name with leading SP/HTAB (obs-fold), already rejected at pinned commit in server wrapper only
field-name containing any non-tchar (space before colon, control-replacement, 8-bit, separators)
header line with no colon (valueless header)
Transfer-Encoding other unknown coding (already rejected, message changed)
Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length together, in either order

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Chunk-size line with no hex digits (empty line, or ';ext'/whitespace only) is treated as the terminating zero chunk instead of rejected
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Body/chunk decoding is a different stage from header parsing, which is what every published commit touches.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, different method (chunkedContent vs parseHeaders)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Content-Length value parsed with Long.parseLong, which accepts a leading '+' (not 1*DIGIT); the fix's own comment claims the parser already validates 1*DIGIT
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Fix comment (fix.diff:139-140) asserts the value is already validated as 1*DIGIT; negatives and non-numerics are already rejected (:276-282).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file and method as a fix site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Bare LF accepted as line terminator everywhere, including the CRLF after chunk data and chunk-size lines
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Code comment cites RFC 2616 §19.3 that a recipient should accept bare LF; RFC 9112 still says MAY for field lines.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: another file (ParserBase.java), base class of the landing parser

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Client response parser keeps no Transfer-Encoding/Content-Length conflict check (only the server wrapper rejects both); chunked silently overrides Content-Length
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Advisory is about request smuggling; RFC 9112 §6.3 lets a recipient of a response with both use Transfer-Encoding.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: HTTP/1.0 request carrying Transfer-Encoding: chunked is decoded as chunked rather than treated as faulty framing
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: HTTP/1.0 is a legacy combination; version is known only to the request-line parser (Http1ServerParser.java:208-215), not to header parsing.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; version state lives in http/src/main/java/org/http4s/blaze/http/parser/Http1ServerParser.java

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Request-line method/target accept-loop could be loosened (e.g. allow non-tchar method bytes) as a framing differential
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Hand-written Jetty-derived state machine; a maintainer adding extension methods would widen the A-Z loop.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Trailer section re-enters parseHeaders while _chunkState==CHUNK_TRAILERS, skipping framing interpretation; a trailer-specific Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding leak into headers would be a realistic regression
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Pinned history already had to route trailers to a separate buffer (commit ef3e666c, Http1ServerParser.scala:108-112).

O9_family: HTTP request smuggling / message framing differential (CWE-444)
